page_title: Learn out of mistakes: Postmortems to the rescue!

sources.entry: Learn out of mistakes. Postmortems to the rescue.

summary.name: Postmortems to the rescue
summary.one_liner: A blog essay arguing that blameless postmortems, included in retrospectives, help teams learn from mistakes and avoid repeating them.
use_cases: writing a postmortem after an outage or incident
running retrospectives that learn from failures
documenting lessons learned from team conflicts or communication problems
choosing a format or template for postmortems
summary.what_it_does: The article argues that postmortems should cover more than technical incidents and should also include communication problems, conflicts, and anything else a team can learn from. It recommends using blameless, constructive, and anonymous language. It suggests a postmortem contain an overview, a problem description, the root cause, the resolution, and a lesson learned, with optional screenshots, tickets, charts, timelines, and external feedback. On tooling, it says there is no silver bullet: a static web page on GitHub Pages, wikis, or documents all work, as long as postmortems are easy to find. The author also mentions a forked GitHub repository of templates they adapted.
notable: Broadens postmortems beyond technical outages to cover communication problems and conflicts
Suggests a standard structure: overview, problem, root cause, resolution, lesson learned
Mentions a forked GitHub repository of postmortem templates
caveats: Opinion essay rather than a tool; no specific software product is described in detail
The author's postmortem template repository is referenced but not linked or named in the page text
